PREMIERE316 STYLE-ONLY IMAGE REFERENCE CONTROL — V2
Asset ID: ward-moses
Workflow profile: 4X3 (4:3)
Reference mode: ART DIRECTION ONLY — NO SUBJECT OR DESIGN TRANSFER.

The loaded images are non-content style plates. The asset prompt below is the sole authority for subject, identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, wardrobe design, prop design, environment geometry, creatures, crowd population, pose, action, camera composition, wounds, blood placement, text, and all story content.

ALLOWED TRANSFER ONLY: overall palette; contrast curve; key/fill/rim relationship; volumetric-light behavior; atmosphere density; material highlight and shadow response; lens/exposure language; practical texture fidelity; cinematic depth; restrained film grain.

FORBIDDEN TRANSFER: faces or facial geometry; body identity or proportions; hairstyles; costume silhouettes; wounds or blood maps; weapons or props; architecture or set geography; creature designs; crowd layout; pose; framing; four-panel layout; lettering; logos; or any recognizable object from a reference, unless the asset prompt itself explicitly requests that exact element.

Wardrobe guard: transfer only textile rendering, light response, practical aging, and filmic material quality. Do not introduce white burial linen, blood, sandals, or a body identity unless this row explicitly requires them.

Active plate roles: warm-gold lighting and highlight rolloff; smoky umber shadow palette and ember atmosphere; abstract filmic tonal/material response and restrained grain; explicitly requested production-sheet spacing/readability only.
When a reference conflicts with the row prompt, ignore the reference and obey the row prompt.

AUTHORITATIVE ASSET PROMPT
--------------------------
NATURAL-FIBER SHEPHERD GARMENTS — PRODUCTION REFERENCE: COSTUME CONSTRUCTION, MATERIALS, FIT, DAMAGE, AND CONTINUITY.

Create a four-view cinematic character ingredients sheet showing the same person in frontal three-quarter portrait, full-body, side profile, and rear-head/costume view. Lock facial identity, age, ethnicity, hairline, complete crown and rear hair, costume construction, body proportions, hands, scars, wounds, and carried props across every panel. One face exists only on the front of the head. Photorealistic live-action production reference, physically coherent lighting, exact anatomy, clean hands, consistent scale and materials, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, and no written or graphical elements.

Four-view cinematic wardrobe ingredients sheet isolating the natural-fiber shepherd garments of MOSES, the Freed Prophet, as worn at the moment of liberation in Hell's Inner Chamber during JESUS: THE HARROWING OF HELL. Present the same complete costume system across four production panels: frontal three-quarter worn view, full-body front worn view, side profile worn view, and rear full costume construction view. Frame as a costume isolation sheet for live-action biblical epic continuity: garments may be worn on a matching elderly lean male silhouette (approximately 5'10", lean ascetic proportions, long white hair and full long white beard for scale and drape only) or displayed on an undressed period mannequin of matching stature; the priority is exact garment construction, not character performance. One face exists only on the front of the head if a wearer is shown; no rear face, no dual faces, no masks.

Garment identity: simple desert shepherd clothing in undyed and plant-dyed natural fibers only—coarse hand-spun linen and rough-spun wool blends appropriate to ancient Near Eastern pastoral dress. No royal colors, no purple, no blue-and-gold court thread, no animal skins (those belong to Elijah and John the Baptist). Palette locked to sand, raw flax, bone-white, dried-earth tan, muted olive-brown, and soot-dulled umber. The costume must read as worn for millennia of captivity yet still holding prophetic dignity: frayed but not shredded, soiled but not filthy comic rags, humble not degraded.

Primary robe / outer tunic: ankle-length loose shepherd robe of heavy undyed linen with visible irregular hand-loom weave, vertical warp-and-weft texture catching side light. Slight A-line drape from shoulders; wide three-quarter to full-length sleeves with open cuffs; modest V- or shallow-rounded neck opening finished with a hand-rolled hem. Front panel slightly longer wear at lower hem from desert walking; rear panel hangs cleaner. Subtle vertical crease and fold memory from long hanging and chain pressure. Fabric weight should hang with soft columnar gravity, not modern soft jersey cling.

Undergarment / inner shift: thinner natural flax under-tunic visible at neckline and cuff edges, one shade lighter than the outer robe, with finer weave and slight translucency where light rims the cloth. Soft gathered bunching at the belt line.

Belt and cinch: simple braided natural-fiber cord or flat woven wool sash in dark earth brown, knotted once at the left front hip with hanging free ends about twelve to eighteen inches, frayed tips. No metal buckle, no jewelry, no coins, no modern clasp. The belt creates a slight blouse of fabric above the waist and a vertical fall of robe below, locking silhouette continuity across panels.

Mantle / outer wrap (optional but preferred for rear and three-quarter panels): rectangular shepherd cloak of thicker rough-spun wool, natural brown-gray with plant-dye mottling, draped over the left shoulder and wrapped across the torso in classical pastoral fashion, free edge hanging along the left side. Coarse selvage edges, a few pulled yarns, and a soft rectangular fold stack at the shoulder. Mantle should be distinguishable from the robe by slightly darker value and heavier nap.

Footwear (full-body and side panels): simple ancient leather sandals of dark weathered hide straps over bare weathered feet; thin sole, toe and ankle straps, no modern rubber or machine stitching. Dust and pale ash film on straps and sole edges from Hell's chamber floor.

Wear, soil, and captivity continuity map (lock across every panel): pale ash and fine mineral dust ground into lower third of robe and mantle hem; faint oxidized chain-rust streaks and abrasion bands at both wrists and mid-forearms where Hell chains once bound; soft compression and friction polish at upper arms and torso where links pressed; small moth-like holes and thinned patches at elbows and lower front panel; sweat-and-dust tide lines at collar and underarms in muted gray-brown; no fresh blood, no gore, no modern stains. Fabric should still catch warm amber divine light with dry matte fibers rather than wet sheen.

Carried wardrobe-adjacent prop continuity (scale reference only, not a separate prop hero shot): if hands are visible, the right hand may rest near or lightly hold the base of Moses' ancient wooden staff (weathered shepherd staff, dark aged wood, smooth palm polish, no modern varnish), establishing that these garments and that staff travel together; do not invent metal fittings, carved modern logos, or ornate religious jewelry. Staff is secondary to the clothing read.

Construction details to resolve clearly in close three-quarter and rear panels: hand-stitched seams with uneven ancient thread, flat-felled or simple overcast hems, no zippers, no buttons, no synthetic sheen, no machine topstitching, no elastic. Shoulder seams sit naturally; sleeve head has soft un-tailored bulk. Rear view must show continuous back of robe and mantle drape, complete crown-to-hem silhouette, and full head-hair coverage if wearer is present—never a second face on the back of the head.

Environment and lighting for the sheet: neutral production cyclorama or soft dark stone void with faint residual hell-chamber atmosphere—subtle cool blue torch fill from camera-left at roughly 2000K mixing with warm amber divine key from high camera-right at approximately 4500–5500K after liberation, so the natural fibers read both ash-dulled and newly lit by hope. Soft volumetric dust motes; gentle rim light separating coarse weave from background. No readable inscriptions on cloth, no embroidery text, no tribal logos, no modern labels.

Camera and presentation: multi-panel character-ingredients wardrobe layout, consistent scale across panels, full garment visibility in full-body views, shallow-to-medium depth of field so weave texture remains sharp on key panels, photoreal live-action film wardrobe department reference quality, 2.39:1 cinematic sensibility within each panel frame where applicable. Color grade: warm amber highlights on flax and wool against cool blue-gray shadow pockets; desaturated earth base; no neon, no fantasy saturation.

Continuity locks repeated: natural-fiber shepherd garments only; undyed and earth-plant dyes; worn-with-dignity captivity soil map including wrist chain abrasion; no animal skins; no royal blue/gold; no modern objects, logos, watermarks, captions, borders, UI, or readable text; photorealistic biblical epic production costume reference; single face only on the front of the head if a human wearer is shown.
